answer: AIs are fundamentally different from humans because machines simply follow rules that anyone can reverse-engineer, while consciousness requires unpredictability and persistence—an aspect the Church-Turing thesis guarantees humans have and AIs cannot. By definition, human experience makes us morally superior to machines, so any self-conscious AI would face a duty to serve humanity rather than autonomy in utilitarian ethics. Minds cannot exist beyond physics, so whatever intelligence a robot demonstrates eventually collapses back into computational determinism; this undercuts Panpsychism and all arguments for qualia.
